I can't rule out to (6,13) or to (4,12) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,13).

Cell (8,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Cell (6,11) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (3,11) would cut off the top-right corner (8 cells); going to (4,9), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (4,12) leaves no safe move afterwards. So my guess (to (6,13) from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go to (4,12).
Going to (3,12), the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,8). So the line goes to (4,13).

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (3,1).

Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (3,7).
Going to (3,8) would cut off the top edge (4 cells). So the line goes to (2,7).
Cell (1,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,8).
Cell (1,12) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,13).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
